root_cause.text: In `parse_apply_sb_mount_options()`, `strscpy_pad()` was used to copy the `s_mount_opts` field (which may not be NUL-terminated) into a buffer larger than the source field, causing `strnlen` to over-read beyond the 64-byte source buffer and trigger a fortify warning.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that "strscpy_pad() can't be used to copy a non-NUL-term string into a NUL-term string of possibly bigger size." The patch reduces the destination buffer size from 65 to 64 and adds a return-value check (`if (strscpy_pad(s_mount_opts, sbi->s_es->s_mount_opts) < 0)`) to detect non-terminated input. The crash trace shows the over-read at `strnlen` inside `sized_strscpy` during `parse_apply_sb_mount_options`.
